ai.title: New agent architecture: research-implement-orchestrator
ai.summary: Introduced `research-implement-orchestrator` (Claude Sonnet 4.5) and `base2-implementor` (GPT-5) to decompose coding tasks into research and implementation layers. `base2-implementor` orchestrates specialized sub-agents for planning, editing, and reviewing, while `task-researcher` generates structured reports on key facts and relevant files. Eval configs updated to test these new agents against `add-custom-tools` task.

ai.title: Add gpt-5-pro planner agent to base2 orchestrator
ai.summary: New `create-plan-gpt-5-pro` agent uses `openai/gpt-5-pro` to generate and select optimal implementation plans. Registered in `.agents/base2/base2-with-pro-planner.ts` `spawnableAgents` list, enabling Buffy orchestrator to spawn this planner after context gathering. Planner operates tool-free, outputting single best plan per priority-ordered principles. Scope limited to internal agent definitions; no user-facing UI or CLI changes.

eli5.text: The assistant now has a new helper that uses a more advanced model to think through the best ways to solve a coding task before starting. When the main orchestrator gathers information about a request, it can now summon this planner to compare five different approaches and pick the simplest one that still meets all requirements. This only affects internal agent definitions used by the development tooling; there are no visible changes to the user interface or command-line commands, so you wouldn't notice it directly unless you're looking at the backend wiring.

ai.title: Add base2-with-task-researcher agent and update task-researcher schema
ai.summary: New `base2-with-task-researcher.ts` defines 'Buffy the Orchestrator', a Claude Sonnet 4.5 agent that manages complex coding tasks via layered sub-agent spawning. `task-researcher.ts` updated to enforce structured output requiring `analysis`, `keyFacts`, and `relevantFiles`, while enabling `includeMessageHistory` and removing `maxContextLength` param. Old `base2-implementor.ts` renamed to `base2-implementor-gpt-5.ts`.

eli5.text: A new AI coding assistant called Buffy the Orchestrator is now live to manage complex programming tasks, which means the system can now break down big coding jobs into smaller research and implementation steps automatically. Buffy uses a structured research agent that returns required analysis, key facts, and relevant files, so the quality of task breakdown is now enforced rather than optional. This affects internal coding workflows starting today, and you would notice if you asked the system to tackle a large multi-step development task, it now routes through Buffy's layered planning approach instead of a single direct agent.

ai.title: Rename internal agent IDs and files
ai.summary: Internal agent definitions renamed in `.agents/`: `base2-max` to `base2-alloy`, `create-plan-gpt-5-pro` to `planner-pro`, `base2-with-pro-planner` to `base2-with-planner-pro`. File names and `id` fields updated to match new naming convention. Scope limited to repo internal agent configs.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the labels used to identify three internal helper agents were changed to match a clearer naming style. If you peeked at the agent configuration files, you'd see that one agent formerly called by a product-name label is now called by its role-based label, and the two others had their identifying labels swapped for more consistent names; every reference between the files was updated to point at the new labels. This is purely internal housekeeping, the helpers still do the same jobs, just under tidier names, with no change to what they can do for you today.

ai.title: Add base2 orchestrator with planner-pro
ai.summary: New base2 agent definition `Buffy the Orchestrator` added at `.agents/base2/base2-with-task-researcher-planner-pro.ts`, using `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`. It spawns `task-researcher` and `planner-pro` among other tools to handle complex coding tasks. `planner-pro` system prompt updated in `.agents/planners/planner-pro.ts` to reflect correct agent name. Scope limited to internal agent definitions.

eli5.text: A new internal assistant named "Buffy the Orchestrator" is now available to help handle complex coding tasks by coordinating several specialized helpers. When assigned a tricky coding job, Buffy can call in a task researcher to investigate the problem, a planner-pro to map out the approach, and other tools to search files and write code. Buffy uses a powerful model (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to manage this teamwork. This is a behind-the-scenes addition to the company's agent tooling, so you won't see it directly unless you're working on one of these coding tasks.
